req12.title: Every Forge screen and entity is built to one set of conventions

spec.goal: The owner gave the same UI and build rules again and again on 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-04: no card mosaics, English sentence-case chrome, enums as colour badges, text behind hover, screens built to the prototype, structure from information architecture, shared components, one schema and one pattern. Each criterion below is one of those rules, quoted from the feedback item that carries it, so every UI issue can trace a criterion to it and a judge can give it a verdict.
scopeIn: Every web-v2 screen of every project on Forge
Mockups a run produces for the owner
Domain entities built on the dev branch
Every module of packages/core/src and the contracts and web modules that serve it (pattern v2)
personas: Owner and maintainer reviewing Forge screens
Agent run building a screen or a mockup
scopeOut: The product UI of the projects Forge manages (HOP, Autoflow)
The language agents write content in (REQ-13)

revisions.changeSummary: BC-18: 'at most one event per act' becomes 'one event per distinct fact, no fact reported twice', and the unconsumed-event check is named.
revisions.title: Every Forge screen and entity is built to one set of conventions
revisions.reason: ISS-1175 measured the whole core integration suite: 1,962 of 12,438 transactions emit more than one outbox event, in 75 shapes. Most report distinct facts that must commit together (a park and its question, a merge mark and its audit comment, a cut and the tag it owes), so 'at most one event per act' cannot hold without splitting acts into halves that can be left apart. The rule that matters is that no fact is said twice. Five shapes do say one fact twice (a domain alias beside a transition event, a refresh beside the event it repeats), and they leave as their own issue.
revisions.acceptReason: Signed by the forge master under the owner's standing direction of 2026-11-09: each real gap in the older requirements leaves as its own work. Agents keep a requirement in line with a direction already given (decision-authority). Measured on the whole core integration suite (ISS-1175): an act that reports distinct facts emits one event per fact by design, so the criterion now says that, and no fact may be said twice.

criteria.body: Flat layout: no screen groups content in bordered cards or boxed sections, nests a box inside a box, or puts a shadow on a content group. Regions are told apart by background tone and one hairline (region tone #FBFAF8 against #FFFFFF, group and table header rows #F5F3EF), never by outlines and never on a cream base. Chips may stay as status markers; a banner is one tinted line. Owner, 2026-10-03: "hạn chế dùng style chia card section quá nhiều… cảm giác UI bị tách nhiều lớp quá"; "Không chia section card nhưng vẫn nên dùng màu nền".

English sentence-case chrome: Forge's own chrome (navigation, titles, tabs, column headers, buttons, badges, tooltips, banners) is English in sentence case, never uppercase-tracked mono headers and never lowercase ids. Content a person or an agent writes may be in any language. Owner, 2026-10-03: "mấy cái tiêu đề hệ thống là dùng tiếng Anh, nội dung thì có thể là tiếng Việt nhưng thuộc về forge UI thì phải là tiếng anh".

Enums are colour badges: a fixed enum value is drawn as a badge (a dot or icon plus a sentence-case label) from its contracts tone map, the same badge on every screen; snake_case and kebab-case values appear only in tooltips and code. Owner, 2026-10-03: "với mấy cái cố định enum thì có thể dùng màu sắc badge để tạo thói quen mắt nhìn cho người dùng" (FB-9).

Progressive disclosure: a screen shows what the viewer acts on. Explanations, guard text, ids, absolute timestamps, evidence detail and long descriptions sit behind a tooltip, a hover card or an expander; a title carries no subtext line and no page carries a breadcrumb. Owner, 2026-10-03: "không phải cứ đổ text hết ra UI là xong, nó sẽ làm loang các thông tin thực tế mà người xem cần xem".

Prototype fidelity: a built screen is judged against its forge-prototype.html route, not against "it renders". The run that builds it compares its own screenshots side by side with the prototype before it merges, and each divergence is either fixed or named in its report. Owner, 2026-10-03: "Requirements build lên đang khá tệ, tệ hơn rất nhiều so với bản design" (FB-1); 2026-10-04: "xem còn phần nào đã mockup mà không làm theo nữa không".

Structure comes from information architecture: headings in the primary text colour with a clear size step, labels at 4.5:1 contrast or better, a sticky facts rail the main column never repeats, each fact and each action shown once with one primary action in the header, tabs instead of one endless scroll on a long detail page, and a named back control ("← Requirements") on every detail page. Owner, 2026-10-04: "bạn có thói quen dùng section lạm dụng giờ không dùng cái là thấy bạn làm UI bối rối về việc sắp xếp thông tin" (FB-2).

Component-first: lists, peeks, detail headers, facts rails, detail tabs, enum badges and waiting-on cells are the shared GroupedList, PeekPanel, DetailHeader, FactsRail, DetailTabs, EnumBadge and WaitingOn components; a screen still holding its own copy is moved onto the shared one in the same change. Owner, 2026-10-04: "UI này làm thì follow hướng làm component giúp tôi nhé".

One build pattern: every module of packages/core/src, and the contracts and web modules that serve it, follows docs/conventions/domain-entities.md (pattern v2), with its enums, refusal codes, request schemas, response shapes, status machines and event types declared once in contracts. Code that breaks a rule is a Wrong marker in the reconciliation flow and is rebuilt to the rule, not patched; scripts/check-module-shape.mjs reports the rules a script can read. A run that diverges names the divergence in its report. Owner, 2026-10-03: "mấy cái build thì cần có schema định nghĩa rõ ràng và pattern rõ ràng đấy chứ đừng build mỗi nơi 1 style" (FB-8); 2026-10-04: "Logic tôi thấy chưa sạch sẽ và build pattern chưa ổn".

Diagram lines say what the relationship is: a line between two boxes carries the relationship's own words from the design, never a count such as "4 links"; a line that merges several relationships shows the first one's words and "+N more", and a hover lists every one with its technology. No label overlaps another label or a box. Owner, 2026-10-04: "Cách vẽ System overview đang lộ ra khá nhiều vấn đề và logic vài chỗ đang rất rắc rối và pattern chưa clean."

Diagrams are laid out by a layout engine, not by hand: boxes and lines come from one deterministic layered layout with orthogonal routing, so a line runs directly between its two ends and never wraps around the frame on a hand-routed bus. A folded group shows its own name and a count chip, never its kind as its name and never a stacked border; the counts a screen states beside the diagram are derived once, by the stage that reads the design. Owner, 2026-10-04: "Cách vẽ System overview đang lộ ra khá nhiều vấn đề và logic vài chỗ đang rất rắc rối và pattern chưa clean."

Module kinds: every directory under packages/core/src is exactly one kind, kernel (job, session, run and issue machines, the transition engine, leases, evidence and records, retry, escalation, the outbox), domain, read-model, adapter, door (REST mount registry, MCP registry, WebSocket, inbound webhooks, CLI shapes) or platform, declared in packages/core/src/modules.json. A directory with no kind is a finding.

Dependency direction (scripts/lib/module-boundaries.mjs:MAY_IMPORT): door imports door, read-model, domain, kernel, adapter ports and platform; read-model imports read-model, domain, kernel and platform; domain imports domain, kernel, platform and adapter ports; kernel imports only kernel and platform; adapter imports only adapter and platform; platform imports only platform. Nothing imports upward and no two modules import each other in a cycle; a need that points upward goes through a port the composition root fills at boot (<context>-ports.ts) only where the answer is needed inside the act's transaction; every other upward need goes through an outbox event.

Public face: each kernel, domain, read-model, adapter and door module exposes exactly one index.ts, and no other module imports a file behind it. Platform modules are leaves and are imported file by file.

Table ownership: every table is owned by exactly one module, listed under its owns in packages/core/src/modules.json, and only that module inserts, updates or deletes the table, by drizzle or raw SQL. Another module reads through the owner's read functions and writes by calling the owner's service.
No database queries in routes: a route file validates its input, calls one service or read function and answers; it holds no db or tx call.

One refusal body: a write a rule refuses answers the envelope { error: { code, message, refusals[] } } from both REST and MCP, its codes declared as as-const arrays in contracts and never in core. Its status says what the caller does next, from contracts/src/refusal.ts:REFUSAL_STATUSES only: 422 by default, 409 re-read and retry, 503 wait for an operator, 403 stop asking, 404 the row is not there, 400 fix the request; 401 and 429 are transport. A rule refusal is never an error class, an HTTPException or thrown text.

Status machines as data: each status machine is declared in contracts as { states, edges: [{ from, to, act, permission, guard }] } and checked against its approved state-machine design; the status column CHECK is built from it. Only the one kernel transition writes a status, with compare-and-set, one record and one outbox event in one transaction. A derived phase is computed in one read-model function, never stored and never a SQL view plus an override. A retired status value is refused by name; the kernel never maps an old status onto a new one (the 17-to-10 legacy map is deleted on dev, owner 2026-10-04).

One durable outbox: a fact another module reacts to is an outbox event written in the act's transaction and typed in contracts; the in-memory hooks bus is retired. An event nobody consumes is not emitted, and a check refuses an event type naming no consumer by name; a subscription to an event nobody emits is removed. One act yields one record, and one event per distinct fact it reports: no fact is reported by two events for the same subject.

Read models: every derived fact a screen or an agent reads (standing, waiting-on, counts, coverage, changed-since-plan, passing, needs-you, the system graph) is computed by exactly one core read model answering one shared contracts shape, and any gate on the same fact applies the one predicate declared in contracts. web-v2 renders, sorts and groups what a read model answered and derives no domain fact itself.

document.title: Feedback lifecycle
document.summary: The statuses of feedback (FB-n). Stored: new, triaged, reopened, verified, declined; planned and resolved are views. Intake captures a screenshot or recording and the step hit, never required. Two checklists, triage and loop close, are filled by the assistant with no chat; a complete one lets whoever holds the act move it on, and moves nothing by itself. Decline and snooze take feedback.approve.

steps.does: A person files feedback about one target (exclusive arc: requirement, issue, release or workflow; where_seen names the screen), from a chat turn only once they press Record it on its card (chat-turn), or core files it for a breaking contract version (E3). It may carry screenshots or a recording, and the workflow step it hits (beside the status); none is required. Filing it starts the assistant's triage draft at once, with no chat opened (REQ-34 BC-10): feedback-triage steps intake, dedup and suggest. Filing also starts the project's steward (REQ-48 BC-1, BC-4).

Filed, its triage checklist incomplete. The assistant drafts it from requirements, workflows, feedback and releases, never the codebase (BC-11): each answer it fills is an assumption naming its source, with at most three questions left, each with a recommended answer (BC-13..BC-15). Stored. It waits only on the person a blocking question names (BC-1). A holder of feedback.approve, the assistant included where the project grants it, may snooze a new or reopened item to a date (at most 365 days) with a reason; the filer is told why and may lift it. Back in New on that date by the read, no timer.

node.label: New
node.owner: BA assistant (draft); whoever a blocking question names

steps.does: The triage checklist: kind; requirement or none; violated criterion or none; severity; reproduced with evidence; route. Short form (BC-6): a bug against an existing criterion needs three answers, the criterion, a reproduction with evidence and a severity; kind is bug, the requirement is the criterion's and the route is an issue on it. Every door asks the same questions (BC-2). The route follows from the answers by the table in feedback-triage step decide. A screenshot or recording may be the evidence a reproduction cites, never the only evidence taken; an item without one is triaged the same.

conditions.when: every answer is given, by the assistant, the reporter or a member, in the full form or the three-answer short form
conditions.result: triaged by whoever triages it, a holder of feedback.approve, the assistant included where granted, in the triage act; nothing triages it by itself (BC-20)

conditions.when: a question the record cannot answer and that changes the route or the outcome (no reproduction for a bug, which requirement it is about)
conditions.result: stays new, waiting on the person who can answer, naming the question (BC-1)

conditions.when: a question that does not block
conditions.result: takes its recommended answer, shown on the item as an assumption with its source; a later answer corrects it (BC-24, BC-26)

conditions.when: the project setting asks a person to agree to triage
conditions.result: waits on a holder of feedback.approve to agree; the agree reads the checklist, never a bare route (BC-25)

steps.does: The triage checklist is complete and the route it gives is written: issue, upgrade issue for a contract change, requirement revision, new requirement draft, answer, or duplicate_of a root. Every answer stays visible on the item, each assumed one marked with its source (BC-26). Stored. The author is told (BC-21). A route to a draft issue stays here, stuck, read as waiting for someone to take on that issue; the steward opens the draft where it may, else asks (REQ-48 BC-5, BC-9).

node.label: Triaged
node.owner: Its triager, in the triage act, or the agreeing person where the setting asks

steps.does: A view, not stored: the route is written and its target is not done, and every carrier issue is past draft. A carrier at draft is no plan: the item reads triaged, grouped Stuck, waiting for someone to take on ISS-n (REQ-48 BC-9). Its wait is the carrier's own standing, rolled up (BC-8), stuck when the carrier is. A duplicate reads its root's phase. At awaiting_release it waits on whoever makes the release.

A view, not stored (Q1): the linked work shipped (issue closed, or the requirement delivered at the revision that took the change), or the answer is stored on the item. A duplicate is resolved when its root is. Loop close, question one: every reporter with a bell is told once, naming what shipped, and asked whether the problem is gone (BC-21). After the release the steward judges the violated criterion on the running build and tells each reporter with that evidence (REQ-48 BC-10).

node.label: Resolved (view)
node.owner: Forge core (tells the reporter); the reporter (answers)

steps.does: Loop close, question two: is the problem gone? Asked of the reporter once resolved; anyone on the project may answer, the decision recording who. A confirm made on the fix's preview answers it where the shipped change has the patch id they saw. After the project's window (feedback.verifyWindowDays, default 7, 1 to 90) with no reply, core reads the record (the violated criterion's latest verdict on the running build, and any feedback, reopen or regression since) and writes it on the item for a feedback.approve holder to answer from. Fast delivery: the ship verifies it.

node.label: Is the problem gone?

conditions.when: fast delivery, and the carrying issue shipped with its criteria met
conditions.result: verified by the ship, recorded with the version; the reporter is told and can reopen it

conditions.when: the reporter, or anyone on the project, says it is gone
conditions.result: verified, recorded as theirs

conditions.when: the reporter says it is not gone, with a reason
conditions.result: reopened (FEEDBACK_REOPEN_REASON_REQUIRED)

conditions.when: the reporter, or a member for them, confirmed the fix in the preview of the issue the item routes to, and the change that shipped has the patch id they saw (loopCloseFromConfirm; the latest confirm wins)
conditions.result: verified (Fixed) or reopened with their note (Not fixed), recorded as theirs, with no ask

conditions.when: no reply within the window, and the record reads it gone: the violated criterion's latest verdict on the running build passes and nothing against it arrived since resolved
conditions.result: stays resolved with that reading and its sources written on it, waiting on a holder of feedback.approve, who verifies or reopens it; nothing verifies it by itself

conditions.when: no reply within the window, and the record cannot say: no criterion, no verdict on the running build, or new evidence against it
conditions.result: stays resolved, waiting on a holder of feedback.approve, naming the question (BC-1)

conditions.when: the project setting asks a person to confirm verification
conditions.result: waits on a holder of feedback.approve to confirm (BC-25)

tests: TEST: Fixed confirmed on a preview whose patch id is the one that shipped -> verified as the confirming person when it reads resolved
TEST: a later Not fixed on the same patch -> the latest confirm wins, the item is reopened with its note
DENY: the confirm names a patch other than the one that shipped, or nothing tells what shipped -> no answer from it, the item asks when it reads resolved

TEST: no reply within the window, the violated criterion passes on the running build and nothing was filed against it since -> the item stays resolved, "the record reads it gone" with those sources written on it, waiting on a holder of feedback.approve
DENY: every cluster timer and outbox consumer runs over that item -> it is not verified; a person's verify or the reporter's confirm closes it

steps.does: The reporter says the fix does not answer it, or the filer reopens a declined item, with a reason. Goes back to triage, keeping its route and decline history; the triage checklist is answered again, the assistant redrafting from the reason. Stored. It is routed again or declined; a verify is refused FEEDBACK_NOT_RESOLVED while it reads reopened.

The loop-close checklist is complete: the reporter was told, and whether the problem is gone was answered by the reporter, by anyone on the project (on behalf of the reporter when not them), or by a holder of feedback.approve from what the record reads, or by the reporter's confirm on the fix's preview; or by the ship under fast delivery. What the record read stays visible; a reporter who still sees the problem reopens it or files new feedback against the same criterion, which the assistant's next draft links (BC-12, BC-26). Stored.

Will not be done: out of scope with no new requirement, or intended behaviour. Declining is a permission, not a person rule: a holder of feedback.approve declines with a reason, a person or an agent, the assistant included where the project grants it that permission. The filer is told why and may reopen it with a reason, which sends it back to triage. Stored. After 180 days its attachments and embedding go; the row stays, and a later reopen keeps the row without them. Done in every read: never late, at risk or stuck.

node.label: Declined
node.owner: A holder of feedback.approve (decided); the filer (may reopen)

steps.does: Beside the status: a holder of feedback.redact deletes what the reporter gave (DELETE …/feedback/:fb/reporter-data): text, screenshots, recordings and other attachments with their bytes and text alternatives, mockups, the embedding, clarification answers and the payloads of suggestions quoting it, keeping the keyed row and its status as a tombstone. Once done, a second is refused FEEDBACK_ALREADY_REDACTED.

Beside the status: screenshots or a recording of what the reporter saw, a reproduce recording a member makes later with its timeline, and, with a workflow target, the step or edge it hits. The item opens on them, above its text and actions, with the step highlighted on that workflow (REQ-35 BC-8). Each has a short text alternative a screen reader reads, never the file name. Anything else names no step, never a guess. None is required; no checklist, guard, turn rule or status reads them as a condition. Added until redacted, which deletes recordings too.

node.label: Screenshot, recording and step (beside the status)
tests: TEST: a member reproduces FB-52 with recording on -> the item lists the recording with its build, its state and a timeline of clicks, page changes, console errors and failed requests
TEST: the recording is 31 days old -> its events are gone (RECORDING_EXPIRED on replay) and its timeline is still read
DENY: a person who is not a member of the project reads the recording -> RECORDING_FORBIDDEN
DENY: the item has no release and none had shipped when it was filed -> PREVIEW_BUILD_UNKNOWN naming a release or a sha to give
DENY: the item's reporter data is redacted -> events and timeline are deleted, the recording reads RECORDING_REDACTED

steps.does: Beside the status: the steward's triage draft (REQ-48 BC-4), a runner job started on filing and on a reopen. It tries a reproduction with evidence on the running build, cites a root cause, merges duplicates and revises the assistant's draft into a triage suggestion with its route and a summary of at most two lines; it accepts its own suggestion only where it holds feedback.approve and no setting asks a person. It asks the reporter at most 3 questions, each with a recommended answer, and never declines.

Beside the status: the steward's note of at most two lines, what happened, what blocks, what is next and by when, citing records, rewritten on each event and shown above the properties with the raw status below (REQ-48 BC-7). A note contradicting the one standing read is refused at write naming the field (BC-8); a project writer may override it.

edges.label: feedback.filed or contract.breaking
edges.condition: names exactly one target in this project (FEEDBACK_TARGET_UNKNOWN / FEEDBACK_TARGET_NOT_IN_PROJECT); kind and severity from the closed sets. Core files one item per consumer per breaking version, deduplicated, kind contract change, deadline from the commitment window (E3); a non-breaking version only notifies
edges.action: on a sensitive_data project the scrubber redacts text on write, before embedding or any LLM call, and flags attachments (Q8); the item is embedded; the assistant drafts the triage checklist at once with no chat (BC-10); where it cannot run, core owes the item to the master on every sweep, most severe first

edges.label: triage.answered
edges.condition: an answer is written to the checklist by the assistant, the reporter or a member; every door writes the same answers (BC-2)

edges.label: feedback.triaged (checklist complete)
edges.condition: every answer of the full form, or the three of the short form, is given; the route is the one the answers give (FEEDBACK_ROUTE_TARGET_MISMATCH); a duplicate's root is not itself one (FEEDBACK_DUPLICATE_CHAIN); where the setting asks, a holder of feedback.approve agreed
edges.action: the route is written in the same act; open questions on the item are closed with their answers; the author is told (BC-21)

edges.label: route.written (view)
edges.condition: the routed_* column the route names is set; route and column must match (FEEDBACK_ROUTE_TARGET_MISMATCH); every carrier issue is past draft: a draft carrier keeps it triaged and stuck (REQ-48 BC-9)

edges.label: target.shipped (view)
edges.condition: the linked issue is closed, or the linked requirement reads delivered at or after the revision that took the change; computed on read, never written

edges.label: question.answered (view)
edges.condition: route is answer and the answer text is stored on the item in the triage act (feedback.answer, scrubbed on a sensitive project; FEEDBACK_ANSWER_MISSING when blank)

edges.label: loop.close asked
edges.condition: it reads resolved; the reporter was told once, naming what shipped, and asked whether the problem is gone
edges.action: core dates the first sight of resolved (resolved_seen_at); a reopen or a re-route clears it, so the window starts again

edges.label: feedback.verified (problem gone)
edges.condition: the reporter or anyone on the project says it is gone; or a confirm made ahead on the fix's preview names the patch that shipped; after the window with no reply the record is read for a holder of feedback.approve, who says it as loop-check draws, and under fast delivery the ship verifies it when its carrier shipped with its criteria met; refused FEEDBACK_NOT_RESOLVED before it reads resolved
edges.action: a decision row records who said it; a confirm is recorded as the person who said it; every reporter with a bell is told once

edges.label: reporter.reopened (problem not gone)
edges.condition: the reporter, or a holder of feedback.approve, says it is not gone and gives a reason (FEEDBACK_REOPEN_REASON_REQUIRED); or a Not fixed confirm with its note names the patch that shipped

edges.label: feedback.declined (from new, triaged or reopened)
edges.condition: a holder of feedback.approve, a person or an agent, the assistant included where the project grants it that permission (PERMISSION_FORBIDDEN otherwise), declines with a reason shown to the reporter (FEEDBACK_DECLINE_REASON_REQUIRED)
edges.action: every reporter with a bell, the duplicates' included, gets one notice naming the reason and that the filer may reopen it

edges.label: feedback.retriaged
edges.condition: the triage checklist is answered again from the reopen reason; the earlier route stays in its history

edges.label: feedback.declined
edges.condition: a holder of feedback.approve, a person or an agent, the assistant included where the project grants it that permission (PERMISSION_FORBIDDEN otherwise); carries a reason shown to the reporter (FEEDBACK_DECLINE_REASON_REQUIRED)
edges.action: every reporter with a bell, the duplicates' included, gets one notice naming the reason and that the filer may reopen it

edges.label: feedback.redacted (beside the status)
edges.condition: the actor holds feedback.redact (PERMISSION_FORBIDDEN); not redacted already (FEEDBACK_ALREADY_REDACTED)
edges.action: the row stays at its status with redactedAt and redactedBy; core withdraws the item's proposed suggestions and purges the payloads of the rest

edges.label: feedback.declined
edges.condition: a holder of feedback.approve, a person or an agent, the assistant included where the project grants it that permission (PERMISSION_FORBIDDEN otherwise); carries a reason shown to the reporter (FEEDBACK_DECLINE_REASON_REQUIRED); a reopened item is declined without being routed again
edges.action: every reporter with a bell, the duplicates' included, gets one notice naming the reason and that the filer may reopen it

edges.label: filer.reopened (declined)
edges.condition: the filer, or a holder of feedback.approve, reopens it with a reason (FEEDBACK_REOPEN_REASON_REQUIRED)
edges.action: the decline stays in the item's history; the assistant redrafts the triage checklist from the reason; the author is told (BC-21)

edges.label: intake.captured, recording.captured (beside the status)
edges.condition: an image or video within the item's caps (FEEDBACK_ATTACHMENT_INVALID naming the type or the cap); a step or edge only with a workflow target, one it draws (FEEDBACK_NODE_NEEDS_WORKFLOW, WORKFLOW_NODE_UNKNOWN); not redacted (FEEDBACK_ALREADY_REDACTED); or a recording a member made in a reproduce preview of the item (RECORDING_FORBIDDEN for a non-member)
edges.action: stored with the item, flagged on a sensitive_data project (Q8); a text alternative left blank reads from the item's title and the attachment's place, and any member may rewrite it; nothing is triaged again; a recording's batches are scrubbed before they are stored

edges.label: feedback.filed or reporter.reopened (beside the status)
edges.condition: the project's steward is on and its daily budget is not spent; one live steward run per item
edges.action: a runner job drafts the triage; its result is a triage suggestion on the item, decided as feedback-triage draws

edges.label: standing.changed (beside the status)
edges.condition: the item's standing moved off its note's, or a steward act ran on it
edges.action: the steward rewrites the note against the current standing; a stale note shows greyed under the standing

edges.label: reporter.reopened (problem returned)
edges.condition: the reporter, or a holder of feedback.approve, reopens a verified item with a reason (FEEDBACK_REOPEN_REASON_REQUIRED)
edges.action: a decision row records who reopened it and why; the item goes back to triage

waitingOn.rule: revision 17 is approved; work that builds it may start

document.title: Feedback triage
document.summary: How one feedback item is triaged and closed across the reporter, the BA assistant, the BA, the master and core. The assistant drafts the triage checklist with no chat; a complete one lets its triager route the item, a person agreeing only where the setting asks. Loop close tells the reporter and writes what the record reads for a person to answer from. Nothing routes or verifies it by itself.

steps.does: The reporter writes what is wrong or wanted, about one requirement, issue, release or workflow, and optionally the step or edge of that workflow (FEEDBACK_NODE_NEEDS_WORKFLOW without one, WORKFLOW_NODE_UNKNOWN for a node it does not draw), and where it was seen.

A breaking contract version files one feedback per consumer per version (deduplicated), kind contract change, deadline from the commitment window (E3). A non-breaking version only notifies; the consumer may adopt it in one act (POST /api/projects/:id/interface/adopt), which moves its interface consumption and its links to that version where every field a link uses is still in it, and names each requirement left stale for a re-pin.

Core writes FB-n at new, from the web (POST /api/projects/:id/feedback), from a chat turn once the person presses Record it on its card (chat-turn), from an agent report promoted to feedback (…/feedback/promote), or once per consumer when a breaking contract version is approved, refusing a target outside the project by name. On a sensitive_data project the text is redacted on write, before embedding or any LLM call, and attachments are flagged (Q8). The write starts the BA assistant at once, with no chat (BC-10). No MCP tool files feedback.
The scrubber from packages/observability, run under the project's sensitive_data policy.

The assistant reads the items nearest to this one as it starts: the item's stored vector compared with the project's of the same model (REQ-8 BC-6), over requirements, feedback and releases. Its draft names duplicates, conflicts, affected workflows and related feedback, each linked (BC-12). Any triager may read the same on demand. At no_egress an agent reads no title, body or answer of an item, and a text search is refused FEEDBACK_SEARCH_WITHHELD.

node.label: Read similar items
node.owner: BA assistant; any triager on demand

steps.does: item_embeddings on pgvector, with model and version, head revision only; vectors of different models are never compared. A degraded write stores no vector and the backfill fills it.

The assistant drafts the triage checklist as a feedback_triage suggestion: kind; requirement or none; violated criterion or none; severity; reproduced with evidence; route. Each answer it fills is an assumption naming its source (BC-13). On the issue route it may carry a diagnosis: the cause and fix read from a reproduce recording's timeline (forge_recording), never its raw events. It asks at most three questions, only ones that change scope or outcome, each with a recommended answer and its effect; none if nothing is worth asking (BC-14..BC-16). A member may answer or correct any line (BC-4).

node.label: Draft the triage checklist
tests: TEST: FB-52 has a reproduce recording that shows a failed request after a click -> the suggestion's issue route carries diagnosis { recording, cause, fix } naming that recording, and the issue it files states the cause, the fix and the recording
TEST: in chat the assistant calls forge_recording with a diagnosis -> the proposal under the reply recommends "Build the fix, ask the reporter to confirm", a button the person presses as themselves
DENY: a diagnosis that names a recording of another item, or none of this item's -> FEEDBACK_DIAGNOSIS_INVALID naming the recordings it has
DENY: a diagnosis on the decline, duplicate or answer route -> FEEDBACK_DIAGNOSIS_INVALID, it rides the issue route only
DENY: a viewer outside the project reads the item's recordings through forge_recording -> RECORDING_FORBIDDEN

steps.does: Exception path: the assistant could not run (a model error, or a no_egress project where no LLM may read the item). Core owes the item to the project master on every sweep, most severe first, naming each FB-n (master verdict work), and the master drafts the same checklist with the same questions. A master placed or resumed while items are owed reads them in its placement brief.

node.label: Master drafts when the assistant cannot

steps.does: Only a blocking question stops the item (BC-1): one the record cannot answer and that changes the route or the outcome, such as a missing reproduction for a bug. It is asked of the person who can answer, the reporter by default, through agent_questions on FB-n, at most three open (BC-14). The answer is written to the checklist and closes the question. A non-blocking question never waits: it takes its recommended answer (BC-24).

node.label: Answers a blocking question
node.trigger: the person a blocking question names answers it on FB-n

steps.does: Core checks the triage checklist on every answer, the same at every door (BC-2): the full form, or the short form for a bug against an existing criterion, which needs only the criterion, a reproduction with evidence and a severity (BC-6). Every answer stays visible on the item, each assumed one marked with its source and corrected by a later answer (BC-26).

conditions.when: every answer of the full form is given: kind, requirement or none, violated criterion or none, severity, reproduced with evidence, route
conditions.result: lets whoever triages it, a holder of feedback.approve, the assistant included where granted, write the route the table gives in the triage act; nothing routes it by itself (BC-20)

conditions.when: short form: kind bug, with the violated criterion, a reproduction with evidence and a severity
conditions.result: complete: the requirement is the criterion's and the route is an issue on it (BC-6)

conditions.when: a blocking question is open
conditions.result: stays new on ask, waiting on the person it names, naming the question (BC-1)

conditions.when: a non-blocking question is open
conditions.result: takes its recommended answer as a marked assumption and goes on (BC-24)

conditions.when: the project setting asks a person to agree to triage
conditions.result: waits on agree (BC-25)

steps.does: Only where the project setting asks for it (BC-25): a holder of feedback.approve, a person or an agent, reads the completed checklist with its assumptions and agrees, or corrects an answer, which the check reads again. Where the setting does not ask, nobody is owed this and the item never waits here.

node.label: Agrees to the triage (where the setting asks)

steps.does: The route table: the route follows from the checklist answers, kind first, and a route the answers do not give is refused by name (FEEDBACK_ROUTE_TARGET_MISMATCH). Decline, which needs a reason, and snooze are acts, not routes. Each is a permission, not a person rule: feedback.approve, held by a person or an agent, the assistant included where the project grants it; the filer is told why and may reopen. The route is written in the triage act with a decision row, and the author is told (BC-21).

conditions.when: kind bug, with a violated criterion
conditions.result: issue on that criterion's requirement, the criterion traced (short form, BC-6)

conditions.when: kind bug or change request on an agreed requirement, with no criterion that covers it
conditions.result: requirement revision: the missing criterion is proposed as a revision_diff

conditions.when: kind idea or change request outside every requirement
conditions.result: new draft requirement

conditions.when: kind question
conditions.result: answer: the assistant drafts it from the record, naming its sources

conditions.when: kind contract change
conditions.result: upgrade issue, with its wait on the contract version (FEEDBACK_ROUTE_TARGET_MISMATCH for any other route)

conditions.when: the checklist names a duplicate
conditions.result: duplicate_of that root

conditions.when: will not do
conditions.result: a holder of feedback.approve, a person or an agent, the assistant included where the project grants it that permission, declines with a reason; its own act, not a route; the filer is told why and may reopen

conditions.when: not now
conditions.result: a holder of feedback.approve, a person or an agent, the assistant included where the project grants it that permission, snoozes it until a date with a reason; the filer is told why and may lift it

conditions.when: the route names nothing that carries it, or two carriers
conditions.result: refused FEEDBACK_ROUTE_INCOMPLETE; an issue route naming no issue files one through issue-lifecycle's ready check, which opens it when complete or names what it lacks

steps.does: In the triage act core files the issue through issue-lifecycle's ready check, or links an existing one (routed_issue_id). It carries what that check asks: requirement_id of the violated criterion's requirement where agreed or accepted, that criterion traced, priority from the severity, category from the kind. A complete one opens in the triage act as the triager's own (issues.admit where asked); an incomplete one stays at draft naming what it lacks and who answers (BC-1, BC-20). The check's hotfix item is open in REQ-34 (question 0769f177), not drawn here. No master hand-off.

In the triage act the consumer's upgrade issue is filed through issue-lifecycle's ready check, or an existing one linked, with its wait on the contract version (contract >= version), never on the provider's issue (E1), due by the end of the commitment window. A complete one is opened in the triage act as the triager's own, an incomplete one names what it lacks. Linking a finished issue (CONTRACT_WAIT_ISSUE_FINISHED) or one already waiting on that contract (CONTRACT_WAIT_DUPLICATE) is refused. Dispatch holds it until an approved version settles the wait.

node.label: File or link the upgrade issue

steps.does: The revision_diff suggestion is taken into a revision draft against the head it was based on (routed_suggestion_id), and requirement-lifecycle's revision check reads it: complete, it waits on its mover to accept it, any project writer, a holder of requirements.approve only where the project setting asks, and the accept makes it current and re-baselines an agreed requirement; nothing makes it current by itself (BC-20, BC-25). The item waits on that, then on the work that delivers the current revision, never on a person once nothing is owed.

node.label: Revision drafted from the proposal
node.owner: Forge core; a holder of requirements.approve only where the setting asks

steps.does: The requirement moved past the proposal's base: refused SUGGESTION_BASE_STALE naming both revisions; a new suggestion is proposed against the head.

Core creates a requirement from the feedback (routed_requirement_id), its title from the item and its reason asked, never required (BC-17). Creating it starts the assistant's draft at once, with no chat (requirement-lifecycle start, BC-10).

node.label: Draft a new requirement
node.owner: Forge core; the BA assistant drafts it

steps.does: The triager sets duplicate_of directly, or accepts a feedback_triage suggestion with route duplicate: the root is not itself a duplicate (FEEDBACK_DUPLICATE_CHAIN), never the item itself (FEEDBACK_DUPLICATE_SELF) and never a declined item (FEEDBACK_DUPLICATE_OF_DECLINED). The item follows its root from here: the root reads every reporter and the evidence merged into it through the duplicate, whose own record stays whole, and the duplicate's reporter gets one notice naming the original.

Route answer: the assistant's drafted answer, naming its sources, is stored on the item (feedback.answer, scrubbed on a sensitive project), where the reporter reads it. Where the setting asks for agree, the answer is posted once agreed.

A holder of feedback.approve declines with a reason: a person, or an agent such as the assistant where the project grants it that permission. Every reporter with a bell, the duplicates' included, gets one notice naming the reason, and the filer may reopen it with a reason, which sends it back to triage (feedback-lifecycle declined).

Not now: a holder of feedback.approve, the assistant included where the project grants it, parks a new or reopened item until a date with a reason (POST …/snooze). The filer is told why and may lift it. It reads Snoozed until, leaves Needs you and the owed drafts, and is back in New on that date by the read, not a timer. A date not to come, more than 365 days away or no reason is refused by name; any triage act clears the snooze.

At any point a triager writes to the reporters: audience this reporter, every reporter merged in, or an internal note. A message to reporters needs feedback.approve and at least one reporter with a bell (FEEDBACK_MESSAGE_NO_RECIPIENT), is previewed exactly as sent (POST …/messages/preview), then sent (POST …/messages). An internal note needs project.write and is never a notice. An empty message is refused FEEDBACK_MESSAGE_EMPTY.

Resolved is a view, not a write (Q1): the linked issue closed, the revised requirement delivered at the revision that took the change, the requirement delivered (every current BC passing), or the answer posted. A duplicate is resolved with its root. Core dates the first sight of resolved (resolved_seen_at).

Loop close, question one, answered by core and required: once it reads resolved, every reporter with a bell is told once, naming what shipped, and asked whether the problem is gone; the notice stays in front of them until they answer or the item is verified (BC-21). A holder of feedback.approve may ask again (POST …/verify-ask). An ask before resolved is refused FEEDBACK_NOT_RESOLVED; the reporter answers directly rather than asking themselves (FEEDBACK_VERIFY_ASK_SELF).

node.label: Tell the reporter; ask if it is gone

steps.does: Loop close, question two, answered by a person: the reporter, or anyone on the project, says the problem is gone, the decision recording who and when; or the reporter, or a holder of feedback.approve, says it is not, with a reason (FEEDBACK_REOPEN_REASON_REQUIRED), which reopens it to triage. Either is refused FEEDBACK_NOT_RESOLVED before the item reads resolved, and settles the reporter's notice. It can be said ahead: a confirm on the fix's preview, bound to its patch id, answers it once the item reads resolved if the change that shipped has that patch id.

node.label: Says whether the problem is gone
tests: TEST: the reporter confirms Fixed in the preview of the issue FB-52 routes to, and the issue ships with that same patch id -> when FB-52 reads resolved it is verified as the reporter, with no ask
TEST: the reporter confirms Not fixed with a note, the same change ships -> FB-52 is reopened to triage with that note
TEST: the issue ships a different patch than the one confirmed -> the confirm answers nothing, the item asks again as before
DENY: a Not fixed confirm with no note -> PREVIEW_CONFIRM_REASON_REQUIRED, nothing recorded
DENY: a confirm on the preview of an issue no feedback item routes to, or on an idea preview -> PREVIEW_CONFIRM_NOT_FIX, nothing recorded
DENY: a confirm by someone who may no longer say it when the item reads resolved -> it closes nothing and the item asks again

steps.does: Nobody answered within the project's window (feedback.verifyWindowDays, default 7, 1 to 90). Core reads question two from the record and writes what it reads on the item with its time: where the violated criterion's latest verdict on the running build passes and no feedback, reopen or regression came since, that the record reads it gone, naming those sources; else why it cannot say. The item stays resolved and waits on a holder of feedback.approve, who verifies or reopens it (BC-1). Nothing verifies it by itself, a record reading it gone included.

node.label: Read the record for a person after the window
node.owner: Core reads; a holder of feedback.approve answers
tests: TEST: past the window, the violated criterion passes on the running build and nothing was filed against it since -> the item stays resolved, reads "the record reads it gone: REQ-n BC-m passes on the running build, ..." and waits on a holder of feedback.approve to say whether the problem is gone
TEST: past the window, the criterion reads failing -> the item stays resolved, the reason written on it, waiting on a holder of feedback.approve
DENY: every cluster timer and outbox consumer runs over an item whose record reads it gone -> it is not verified; only a person's verify, or the reporter's confirm on the fix's preview, closes it

lanes.label: BA assistant
lanes.tooltip: The in-core assistant, started by the item's creation, with no chat. It reads requirements, workflows, feedback and releases, never the codebase (REQ-34 BC-11).

edges.label: to the assistant, redacted, no chat

template.title: Cross-functional process
template.purpose: Use when you are drawing a process across roles you name — a swimlane, a BPMN-lite or UML activity diagram: each lane is a role the design declares in `lanes`, with the blueprint’s steps, gateways and waits.

nodeTypes.label: Evidence
nodeTypes.tooltip: What the customer sees or holds: a letter, a message, a screen.

nodeTypes.label: Frontstage
nodeTypes.tooltip: What staff or the product do before the customer, on a `channel`.

links.tooltip: The screen a digital frontstage is.

nodeTypes.label: Backstage
nodeTypes.tooltip: What staff do out of the customer’s sight.

links.tooltip: The step of the operational flow that does this work.

nodeTypes.label: Support
nodeTypes.tooltip: A system or service the work leans on.

nodeTypes.label: Gateway
nodeTypes.tooltip: A branch: exclusive (one way, by condition) or parallel.

nodeTypes.label: Wait
nodeTypes.tooltip: Waiting on a timer or a message (`trigger`).

edgeKinds.label: Flow
edgeKinds.tooltip: The next step; customers reach systems only through the frontstage.

edgeKinds.label: Handoff
edgeKinds.tooltip: Work passes to another role; the line says who takes it.

edgeKinds.label: Uses
edgeKinds.tooltip: Frontstage or backstage work leans on a support system.

edgeKinds.label: Evidences
edgeKinds.tooltip: What the customer sees of a step.

template.title: State machine
template.purpose: Use when you are drawing the states one thing — a case, a task, an attention item — moves through, the event that moves it (the line’s label), its guard (`condition`) and who may move it. Statecharts are drawn in it; FHIR Task and Encounter have presets.

nodeTypes.label: Initial
nodeTypes.tooltip: Where the machine starts; there is exactly one.

nodeTypes.label: State
nodeTypes.tooltip: A state the subject is in; non-final ones have a way out.

nodeTypes.label: Compound state
nodeTypes.tooltip: A state that holds states of its own.

nodeTypes.label: Parallel region
nodeTypes.tooltip: States that run at the same time.

nodeTypes.label: Choice
nodeTypes.tooltip: A branch on a guard; each way out has its condition.

nodeTypes.label: Final
nodeTypes.tooltip: A state nothing moves on from.

edgeKinds.label: Transition
edgeKinds.tooltip: An event moves it on: event [guard] / action.

edgeKinds.label: After
edgeKinds.tooltip: A timer moves it on: an SLA ran out (`condition`).

edgeKinds.label: Back
edgeKinds.tooltip: An event moves it back to an earlier state (a reopen).
